composition.story: fact(4) can't answer right away, so it calls fact(3). Each call waits on the stack for a smaller one. At fact(1), the base case, the calls stop. The answers then come back up: every waiting frame finishes its multiplication in reverse order. The stack shrinks back to empty, and the final result is 24.

aha.observation: fact(1) returns 1 without calling again. The stack stops growing, so every waiting frame can now finish in reverse order.

parts.presentation: Call stack: fact(4) frame at the bottom, fact(1) frame at the top
Faint outline of the frames from the previous step

controls.label: Step
controls.presentation: Previous / Next buttons that keep their names when disabled; arrow keys also work

controls.label: Reset
controls.presentation: Goes back to the first step

states.label: Call fact(4)
states.sentence: fact(4) isn't the base case, so it pauses and calls fact(3).
states.why: Since n > 1, it needs the smaller answer first.

states.label: Call fact(3)
states.sentence: fact(3) also pauses and calls fact(2). Another frame goes onto the stack.
states.why: Each call works on n − 1, which moves it closer to the base case.

states.label: Call fact(2)
states.sentence: fact(2) pauses and calls fact(1). Three frames are now waiting.
states.why: No frame can finish until a call below it returns.

states.label: Base case fact(1)
states.sentence: fact(1) returns 1 right away. It makes no new call, so the stack stops growing.
states.why: The base case answers directly, which ends the chain of calls.

states.label: fact(2) returns
states.sentence: fact(2) finishes 2 × 1 = 2, and its frame comes off the stack.
states.why: The waiting multiplication now has its missing value.

states.label: fact(3) returns
states.sentence: fact(3) finishes 3 × 2 = 6 and passes it down to fact(4).
states.why: Frames finish in the reverse of the order they were called.

states.label: fact(4) returns
states.sentence: fact(4) finishes 4 × 6 = 24. The stack empties, and the answer is 24.
states.why: The first call to start is the last one to finish.

1.reason: The stack picture with frames growing to the base case and unwinding answers how recursion terminates and returns 24.

2.reason: The aha state s4 is a manual step with no timer, so it holds until the learner clicks Next.

3.reason: The step index is the sole parameter, and each step changes the active frames, readouts and callout.

4.reason: The ghost, callout, readouts and links each bind to declared fields such as previous.active, state.calloutRegion and state.readouts.

6.reason: The story, step labels and frame labels all use the same fact(n) calls and returns in the same order.

7.reason: One picture with a single changing region plus three readouts adds the pending-work product without clutter.

8.reason: Depths 1 to 4 and back, the pending products, and the returns 2, 6 and 24 are all correct; the callout locates the frame and the readouts hold the numbers.
